source.title: Polysemy of Synthetic Neurons Towards a New Type of Explanatory Categorical Vector Spaces
source.authors: Michael Pichat; William Pogrund; Paloma Pichat; Judicael Poumay; Armanouche Gasparian; Samuel Demarchi; Martin Corbet; Alois Georgeon; Michael Veillet-Guillem

record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own measurements of categorical proximity and activation in GPT2-XL, but does not test any listed claim version: it does not audit the stated shares, test explanations on held-out activations, or measure explanation scores on new text.
record.gate_note: The study analyzes GPT2-XL core-token activations and embedding-based proximity to proposed categorical subdimensions. These findings concern neuron polysemy but do not measure the claim versions' specific outcomes. The paper also reviews and cites related work; cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures, in GPT2-XL layer 1, how token activation relates to embedding cosine proximity to 'taken-cluster' subdimensions. It does not audit the share of neurons with one or two jobs, compare models or scale, examine InceptionV1 or recursive generalization, vary architecture or tools, build neuron attribution graphs, or score explanations on held-out text. It proposes an alternative reading of polysemy (intra-neuronal categorical vector space) but gives no result that bears on any listed version. It uses Bills et al. 2023 data only as its source of core tokens.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that a GPT2-XL early-layer neuron can be modelled as an intra-neuronal categorical vector space with a non-orthogonal basis of subdimensions clipped from layer n−1 neurons. Highly activated tokens sit at the intersection of subdimensions and are more monosemous; lower-activated core tokens are more polysemous. They present this as an alternative, not contradictory, view to superposition.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses GPT2-XL core-token sets, taken-clusters, and cosine similarities between GPT2-XL embeddings to measure categorical proximity; it does not use the Qwen3-32B pole audit or held-out explanation-testing procedures.

fits_no_version.finding: In selected GPT2-XL L1 neurons, the 10 most-activated core tokens are closer in embedding space to the neuron's taken-cluster subdimensions than the 10 least-activated (78% of 614 neurons; mean δ=.0274; Cliff's delta .24). On an averaged neuron, activation rank correlates with proximity (tau .78–.85).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within a neuron's top-activating tokens, higher activation goes with more categorical convergence across precursor-derived subdimensions; lower-activation core tokens are more polysemous.

record.problems: The empirical analysis is restricted to GPT2-XL's L1 and selected core-token/taken-cluster subsets. Categorical proximity is operationalized using GPT2-XL embedding cosine similarity; the study does not validate these subdimensions against held-out firing examples or test whether verbal explanations predict activations. The reported PCA includes an averaged-neuron analysis, though the authors also show non-averaged examples.
record.rows_left_out: No additional qualifying results were left out. Related-work results cited in the literature review were not recorded as study results.

untested.parts: All: the Qwen3-32B pole shares (~90% one job, ~7% two related jobs, 2–4% not understood).
All: shares in other models, dense vs mixture-of-experts, scale.
All: InceptionV1 cat/car neuron, pose, recursive generalization vs superposition.
All: effects of architecture, regularization and tools on interpretable share.
All: neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model.
All: whether explanations from activating examples predict firing elsewhere. The study only uses top-100 core tokens and never tests verbal explanations.
All: simulation-based explanation scores on new text.

record.verdict_notes: Analyses are confined to GPT2-XL layer 1 core tokens, using data from Bills et al. 2023 (an original source), used here only as input. The polysemy framing is conceptually adjacent to V3 (polysemy as a shared coherent feature rather than superposition) but involves no vision model and no test of that reading. Averaged-neuron correlations may be inflated by aggregation. Cited literature results are correctly excluded from the rows.

versions.untested_parts: The Qwen3-32B pole shares and the proportion of poles with one, two, or not-yet-understood jobs.
Comparisons across models, dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, or model scale.
InceptionV1's cat-and-car example, pose detection, and recursive generalization versus superposition.
Effects of architecture, regularization, or tool quality on interpretability shares, including the stated InceptionV1-sized estimates.
Whether attribution graphs built from a model's own neurons explain behavior without a replacement model or its reconstruction error.
Whether explanations based on activating examples predict firing on examples they were not written from.
Automated explanation scores from simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: GPT2-XL
rows.operation_detail: Compared activation levels of core tokens with their mean cosine-similarity proximity to up to 10 categorical subdimensions.

conditions.value: 614; each had at least 3 taken-clusters, each with at least 6 taken-tokens, and at least 40 distinct tokens across clusters
100 core-tokens per neuron; compared the 10 least and 10 most activated

rows.measure: Difference in mean dimensional proximity between the 10 most- and least-activated core tokens (δ = smax − smin), and network-level proportion with δ > 0.
rows.value: Mean δ = .0274; 78.0130% of neurons had δ > 0; mean αmin = 1.3843, mean αmax = 3.0218, mean σmin = .3991, and mean σmax = .4265.
rows.note: The reported result is a positive activation–proximity association in the selected GPT2-XL L1 neurons; it is not a count of interpretable jobs or poles.
rows.check: Measures an activation-to-embedding-proximity association among core tokens, not a share of interpretable neurons or explanation accuracy. No version's effect can be read from it. The 'observed' state is relative to the paper's own hypothesis, not to a claim version.

rows.subject: GPT2-XL
rows.operation_detail: Computed Kendall correlations between activation rank and proximity to three categorical subdimensions in an averaged neuron.

conditions.value: 612 neurons associated with exactly 3 taken-clusters, each containing at least 6 tokens
Mean proximity at each token activation rank across the selected neurons

rows.measure: Kendall’s τ between token activation rank and dimensional proximity for each of three subdimensions.
rows.note: This is an aggregate over 612 neurons, described by the paper as correlations on an average neuron.
rows.check: Kendall's tau is computed on an averaged neuron (612 neurons), so it says nothing about per-neuron interpretability shares. Not linked to any version.

rows.subject: GPT2-XL
rows.operation_detail: Conducted PCA on four categorical-subdimension proximity measures for an averaged neuron and examined token activation on the resulting axes.

conditions.value: 463 neurons with exactly 4 taken-clusters, each containing at least 6 tokens
Averaged token proximities across selected neurons; PCA used 100 mean core-token ranks and 4 mean proximity variables

rows.measure: PCA structure of subdimension proximities and association of token activation with the factorial axes.
rows.value: The first factor explained 93.5% of initial variance and the second 4.8%. The paper reports that the first factor represented partial categorical convergence, while the second represented polysemy and divergence. Higher-activation tokens had higher positive values on Factor 1 and higher negative values on Factor 2.
rows.uncertainty: Bartlett’s test p < .0001; KMO = .82; eigenvalues VP1 = 3.74 and VP2 = .19.
rows.locator: Section 4.2, Graph 2 and Graph 4, with accompanying text
rows.note: The paper says Graph 3 showed similar observational trends for individual, non-averaged neurons. This PCA analysis is still a proximity-based measure, not an evaluation of written neuron explanations.
rows.check: PCA of subdimension proximities on an averaged neuron (463 neurons). This is a proximity-structure measure, not a version outcome.
